title: Tabularis Plugin Manifest
description: Runtime schema for a Tabularis driver bundle (.tabularium or legacy manifest.json). For registry publication, use the registry's live merged schema.

id.description: Stable driver identifier used in saved connections and plugin folder names. Optional for legacy compatibility: when absent, identity falls back to name. For registry publication it must match the existing registry slug and ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ (1–64 characters).

name.description: Human-readable display name (e.g. "DuckDB") when id is present. Without id, this is also the legacy plugin identifier and must remain a lowercase slug for registry publication.

description.description: Short description shown in the plugins list.

default_port.description: Default TCP port for the database. Use null for file-based databases.

is_builtin.description: true for built-in drivers shipped with Tabularis. External plugins should omit this field or set it to false.

default_username.description: Default username pre-filled in the connection modal (e.g. "postgres", "root"). Leave empty if there is no conventional default.

executable.description: Relative path to the plugin executable inside the plugin folder (without extension on Linux/macOS; Tabularis appends .exe on Windows automatically).

connection_metadata.description: Opt in to get_connection_metadata, which returns connection-specific capabilities, data_types and type_mappings. Static manifest values remain the fallback.

capabilities.description: Feature flags that control which UI elements Tabularis renders for this driver.

schemas.description: true if the database supports named schemas (e.g. PostgreSQL). Shows the schema selector in the connection UI.

views.description: true to enable the Views section in the database explorer.

materialized_views.description: true to enable the Materialized Views section in the database explorer. The backing RPCs (get_materialized_views, get_materialized_view_columns, get_materialized_view_definition, refresh_materialized_view) are optional: listing falls back to empty results when the plugin does not implement them.

routines.description: true to enable stored procedures and functions in the database explorer.

routine_management.description: true to enable routine management actions (run with parameters, create from template, edit, drop). The backing RPCs (build_routine_call_sql, routine_create_template, get_routine_edit_script, drop_routine) are optional: the host falls back to dialect-neutral SQL when the plugin does not implement them.

triggers.description: true if the driver supports trigger metadata and trigger management RPCs.

file_based.description: true for local file databases (e.g. SQLite, DuckDB). Replaces the host/port fields with a file path input.

in_memory.description: Requires file_based. true if the driver also opens the path ":memory:" as a temporary database that lives in the plugin process (e.g. DuckDB). Adds an in-memory shortcut next to the file path input and skips the file existence check for that path.

folder_based.description: true for plugins that connect to a directory rather than a single file (e.g. CSV plugin). Replaces host/port fields with a folder picker.

connection_string.description: Optional capability for network drivers. Set false to hide connection string import in the UI.

connection_uri.description: Pass the connection URI verbatim to the driver instead of decomposing it into host, port and database fields.

connection_uri_schemes.description: Additional URI schemes handled by this driver, such as jdbc.

connectionString.description: CamelCase alias of connection_string. Optional capability for network drivers.

connection_string_example.description: Optional placeholder example shown in the connection string field (e.g. "postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/db").

connection_string_examples.description: Optional connection string presets shown in the connection form.

identifier_quote.description: Character used to quote SQL identifiers: double-quote for ANSI SQL, backtick for MySQL-style.

sql_dialect.description: SQL dialect preset used by Tabularis for statement splitting, query classification and generated SQL. Oracle-like plugins can use oracle. For an engine no preset describes, set the closest preset here and declare sql_syntax.

sql_syntax.description: Declarative SQL syntax extending a preset, for engines no preset describes (e.g. GoogleSQL). Data only. Every field is optional and overrides one rule of the extended preset; invalid fields are ignored with a warning and never fail loading. Hosts that predate it ignore it and use sql_dialect. See PLUGIN_GUIDE.md#sql-syntax-sql_syntax.

extends.description: Preset to extend. Defaults to sql_dialect.

quotes.description: Replaces the preset's quote rules; each open at most once.

close.description: Defaults to open (] for [); any other value is invalid.

escape.description: double: '' escapes a quote; backslash: \' (no doubling); both; none.

triple_quoted_strings.description: '''…''' and """…""" strings for the ' and " string quotes.

string_prefixes.description: Letter prefixes before a string quote, any case (e.g. r, b, rb, br).

line_comment_requires_space.description: -- needs a following whitespace to start a comment.

script_blocks.description: Procedural BEGIN … END, IF, LOOP, WHILE, REPEAT, FOR and CASE blocks stay one statement.

string_escape.description: How generated string literals are escaped: standard ('') or backslash (\'). On a mysql base, standard is ignored (backslashes stay escaped).

like_escape.description: Whether LIKE … ESCAPE is supported. false: LIKE filters escape wildcards with a backslash and omit ESCAPE.

boolean_literals.description: How Tabularis writes boolean literals in SQL it generates (dumps, Copy as INSERT, filters, notebook cell references). keywords: TRUE / FALSE. numeric: 1 / 0. Omit to keep each generator's default (dumps: TRUE / FALSE on postgres, 1 / 0 elsewhere). Set keywords for an engine without implicit integer-to-boolean coercion (GoogleSQL).

alter_primary_key.description: true if the database supports altering primary keys after table creation.

auto_increment_keyword.description: Keyword appended after the column type for auto-increment columns (e.g. "AUTO_INCREMENT" for MySQL). Empty string if not applicable.

serial_type.description: Replacement data type used for auto-increment columns (e.g. "SERIAL" for PostgreSQL). Empty string if not applicable.

inline_pk.description: true if primary key is defined inline in the column definition (e.g. SQLite AUTOINCREMENT style).

table_query_templates.description: Generate SQL SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE previews through the optional get_table_query_template RPC.

alter_column.description: true if the driver supports ALTER TABLE MODIFY/ALTER COLUMN on existing tables.

create_foreign_keys.description: true if the driver properly supports creating foreign key constraints.

no_connection_required.description: true for API-based plugins that need no host/port/credentials (e.g. public REST APIs). Hides the entire connection form and skips database validation.

manage_tables.description: true if the driver supports table and column management (CREATE TABLE, ADD/MODIFY/DROP COLUMN, DROP TABLE). Does not control index or foreign key operations. Defaults to true.

readonly.description: When true, the driver is read-only: all data modification operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) are disabled in the UI. Table and column management is also hidden regardless of manage_tables. Defaults to false.

supports_ssl.description: true to show the SSL/TLS configuration tab (mode + CA/client cert/key) in the connection modal for this network driver. Defaults to false.

connection_fields.description: Optional presentation overrides for host-owned connection fields. Omitted fields keep the standard Tabularis behavior.

hidden.description: Hide this field for the driver.

interpreter.description: Optional interpreter for script-based plugins (e.g. python3).

settings.description: Optional list of configuration fields the plugin exposes to the user.

explain_parsers.description: Optional EXPLAIN parser bundles supplied by the plugin.

engine.description: Canonical database engine identifier handled by this parser.

format.description: Globally unique raw EXPLAIN wire-format tag.

module.description: Path to the parser IIFE relative to the installed plugin directory.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for format pickers.

type_mappings.description: Optional map of generic inferred type names to driver-specific types. Used by the host to resolve map_inferred_type() locally without an RPC call. Keys are uppercase generic names (e.g. DATETIME, JSON), values are the driver-native equivalents (e.g. TIMESTAMP, JSONB).

data_types.description: List of SQL data types supported by this driver for column creation in the UI.

name.description: SQL type name as it appears in DDL (e.g. "VARCHAR", "BIGINT").

category.description: UI grouping category for this type.

requires_length.description: true if this type requires a length argument (e.g. VARCHAR(255)).

requires_precision.description: true if this type requires a precision/scale argument (e.g. DECIMAL(10,2)).

default_length.description: Optional default length value pre-filled in the UI (e.g. "255" for VARCHAR).
